declaredScopeIssues: Physics: established working fluid mechanics and its advanced continuum continuation remain unfinished. Pressure, flow and diffusion applications appear in physical foundations, physiology, waves and statistical mechanics, but no contract teaches deriving and solving viscous incompressible flow or validating a fluid experiment. These neighboring outcomes do not provide full undergraduate-advanced fluid-mechanics coverage.

Physics: established plasma-physics foundations remain unfinished. Electromagnetism and statistical mechanics do not teach charged-fluid or kinetic plasma models, Debye screening, plasma oscillations and magnetized transport as a coherent graduate capability.

Chemistry: established graduate molecular spectroscopy remains unfinished. The included chemistry/molecular-spectroscopy outcomes provide working first-order interpretation and chemistry/quantum-chemistry provides basic quantum spectra, but no contract teaches multidimensional NMR pulse-sequence reasoning or time-resolved molecular spectroscopic inference at graduate depth.

Mathematics: linear programming has a teaching contract in computer-science/advanced-algorithms, but its only route imposes the complete advanced-algorithm curriculum rather than an independent undergraduate working entry. An accessible linear/discrete optimization route remains to be separated while preserving the graduate guarantees.
interpretation: Structural validity and traceability do not establish completeness or learner readiness. Higher-level sources, alternate paths, and other source outcomes are inspection signals, not automatic defects. Do not delete edges or split decks without evaluating their contracts.

exclusions.subject: mathematics
exclusions.rationale: Derived algebraic geometry, large-cardinal set theory and specialized geometric-analysis research programs are outside this representative progression; they are not assumed prerequisites.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.rationale: Specialized hardware fabrication, production-scale foundation-model infrastructure and every application-specific AI subfield are not cataloged. General architecture, distributed systems and learning foundations are included at their own depths.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.domain: Specialized chemical qualifications and frontier catalogs
exclusions.rationale: Dedicated radiochemical handling, industrial process licensure and exhaustive specialized synthesis families are excluded; general reaction, analytical and catalytic capabilities remain included.

exclusions.subject: physics
exclusions.domain: Additional frontier physical theories and facilities
exclusions.rationale: String theory, full quantum field theory, dedicated accelerator engineering and specialized plasma facilities are outside the representative continuation. Nuclear/particle models and classical field foundations have separate included mappings above.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.domain: Professional qualifications and additional biological specialties
exclusions.rationale: Clinical, veterinary and regulated environmental credentials, organism-by-organism taxonomic catalogs and every frontier synthetic-biology platform are excluded; the corresponding scientific foundations are included above.

outcomes.description: Evaluate real and complex integrals with residues and branch choices; construct elementary conformal maps and use them to solve bounded two-dimensional potential problems.
Prove and apply Cauchy-Riemann, Cauchy integral, power-series and maximum-principle results and classify isolated singularities.

practice: Produce rigorous contour calculations, including vanishing-arc estimates, and map a planar boundary problem to a solvable domain.

includes: Smooth and convex optimization, constrained optimality and implementable solvers

outcomes.description: Establish convexity, derive first/second-order and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and use Lagrangian dual bounds under explicit constraint qualifications.
Implement gradient, Newton, projected-gradient and basic proximal methods; derive elementary convergence bounds and diagnose poor scaling and nonconvex failure.

practice: Implement constrained least-squares and sparse-estimation solvers and compare numerical stopping criteria with provable optimality certificates.

includes: First- and second-order ODEs, linear systems and phase portraits

outcomes.description: Solve separable and linear first-order equations, constant-coefficient second-order equations and forced linear systems using initial conditions, eigenmodes and matrix exponentials.
Construct phase portraits, locate equilibria, classify local stability by linearization and use existence/uniqueness conditions to interpret one- and two-dimensional models.

practice: Derive a forced two-state model, solve its linear case and compare phase-portrait predictions with provided numerical trajectories.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tensors, differential forms, connections and curvature

outcomes.description: Calculate metrics, Levi-Civita connections, geodesics and Riemann/Ricci curvature in Riemannian and Lorentzian examples and connect local curvature with geometric invariants.
Construct manifold charts and tangent/cotangent spaces; transform tensor components, calculate exterior derivatives and pullbacks and apply manifold Stokes' theorem.

practice: Calculate the same curvature invariant in two charts and derive geodesics for a curved surface and a simple Lorentzian metric.

includes: Nonlinear dynamics, numerical time integration, feedback and deterministic state estimation

outcomes.description: Construct state-space and transfer-function models, test controllability and observability, and design pole-placement feedback and Luenberger observers with robustness checks.
Analyze stability with Jacobians and Lyapunov functions, identify elementary bifurcations and implement Euler and Runge-Kutta integration with step-size and stability checks.

practice: Implement a controlled two-state plant, compare open/closed-loop behavior and demonstrate instability caused by delay or an excessive integration step.

includes: Banach/Hilbert spaces, bounded operators, duality and spectral foundations

outcomes.description: Prove completeness and approximation properties in sequence and function spaces; apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping results and distinguish weak from norm convergence.
Analyze bounded and compact operators, adjoints and spectra; prove Hilbert projection and compact self-adjoint spectral results and apply variational solvability arguments.

practice: Prove solvability and stability of an infinite-dimensional variational problem and construct a counterexample when a key hypothesis fails.

includes: Modules, field extensions, Galois theory and finite-group representations

outcomes.description: Prove and apply the Galois correspondence to polynomial solvability and construct finite-group representations and character decompositions over the complex numbers.
Analyze modules over principal ideal domains, exact sequences and tensor products; relate module structure to canonical matrix forms and calculate finite field extensions.

practice: Determine a nontrivial polynomial's Galois group and decompose a finite-group action into irreducible representations with full justification.

includes: Decision and likelihood theory, asymptotic inference, hierarchical Bayes and Monte Carlo

outcomes.description: Construct hierarchical Bayesian models and implement importance sampling, Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs sampling; justify invariant distributions and diagnose convergence and posterior predictive failure.
Analyze sufficiency, information, optimal tests and estimator risk; derive regular likelihood consistency/asymptotic normality and explain failures at boundaries or under misspecification.

practice: Derive an estimator's limiting law and implement a hierarchical posterior analysis, testing both interval coverage and sampling diagnostics.

includes: Real and complex vector spaces, matrices, eigenstructure and least squares

outcomes.description: Construct projections, least-squares solutions and singular-value decompositions and diagnose rank deficiency.
Solve linear systems by elimination and represent linear maps through bases, rank, null spaces, determinants and coordinate changes.
Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors; use inner products, orthogonal/unitary bases and diagonalization of symmetric or Hermitian matrices.

practice: Recover an unknown vector from noisy linear measurements and compare exact, least-squares and rank-truncated solutions.

includes: Measure, Lebesgue integration, continuous probability and limit theorems

outcomes.description: Construct measurable functions and Lebesgue integrals and prove/apply monotone and dominated convergence, product integration and Radon-Nikodym results with explicit hypotheses.

Calculate continuous and joint distributions, conditional expectations and characteristic functions; prove core laws of large numbers and a central limit theorem and analyze elementary Markov chains and martingales.

practice: Write a measure-theoretic proof portfolio and analyze convergence of a stochastic sequence with both theorem hypotheses and counterexamples.

includes: Multivariable differentiation, curves, surfaces and vector integration

outcomes.description: Parametrize curves and surfaces; compute tangent and normal directions, arc length, area and elementary curve and surface curvature.
Calculate gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, total derivatives, constrained extrema and multiple integrals with coordinate changes in two and three dimensions.
Calculate line and surface integrals, divergence, curl and Laplacians in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates and apply Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems.

practice: Represent a three-dimensional field in two coordinate systems and verify an integral theorem on a curved boundary.

includes: Floating-point error, root finding, interpolation, quadrature and numerical linear algebra

outcomes.description: Implement pivoted elimination and QR least squares, use an SVD library transparently, and diagnose ill-conditioning through residuals and perturbation experiments.
Implement bisection, Newton iteration, polynomial interpolation and composite quadrature; derive elementary error bounds and distinguish conditioning, truncation and roundoff.

practice: Implement a tested numerical library and construct cases where a small residual conceals a large solution error.

includes: Finite probability, conditional probability, descriptive statistics and sampling

outcomes.description: Summarize data graphically and numerically; distinguish sampling from measurement bias and use a supplied normal model or simulation to describe sampling variability.
Construct finite sample spaces, apply conditional probability and Bayes' rule, and calculate expectations and variances for Bernoulli, binomial and discrete models.

practice: Analyze a diagnostic-test example and use a spreadsheet sampling experiment to explain base-rate effects and sample-size dependence.

includes: Logic, sets, relations, induction, graphs and counting

outcomes.description: Construct sets, relations, functions, finite graphs and trees; count finite arrangements and solve elementary recurrences.
Translate quantified statements and prove or refute claims using direct proof, contradiction, contraposition and ordinary or structural induction.

practice: Write a proof portfolio including an induction argument, a graph invariant and a counterexample to a plausible false claim.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, units, coordinate geometry and complex numbers

outcomes.description: Calculate with fractions, powers, logarithms and units; solve algebraic equations and interpret linear, exponential and trigonometric functions in tables and graphs.
Use Cartesian and polar coordinates, similarity, areas and volumes; calculate with two- and three-dimensional vectors, dot and cross products, and rectangular or polar complex numbers.

practice: Build and check a unit-consistent scaling model from measurements; solve a coordinate-geometry problem using both diagrams and algebra.

includes: Completeness, metric limits, continuity and convergence of functions

outcomes.description: Distinguish pointwise from uniform convergence and prove or refute interchange of limits, derivatives, sums and integrals under explicit hypotheses.
Use completeness, compactness and epsilon-delta arguments to prove sequence, continuity, differentiation and Riemann-integration results on real intervals and metric spaces.

practice: Write complete proofs and counterexamples for a sequence of approximation claims, identifying exactly where uniformity is needed.

includes: Intervals, tests, simple regression, randomization and study design

outcomes.description: Calculate and interpret confidence intervals and one- or two-sample tests using normal, t, binomial or randomization procedures; distinguish effect size, uncertainty and multiplicity.
Fit and check simple linear regression using stated formulas or a statistical tool; identify confounding, pseudoreplication and appropriate randomization or blocking.

practice: Analyze a randomized comparison and an observational dataset, including residual plots, a tool-based bootstrap and a written limits-of-inference statement.

includes: Multivariate regression, generalized linear models, likelihood and model validation

outcomes.description: Implement bootstrap and permutation procedures, cross-validation and multiple-testing control; diagnose leakage, misspecification, confounding and unstable coefficients.

Construct Gaussian linear, logistic and Poisson models in matrix notation; derive likelihoods and gradients, fit them using a documented optimizer and interpret interactions, regularization and uncertainty.

practice: Build a reproducible regression analysis from raw data, implement resampling and defend the choice of predictive versus causal interpretation.

includes: Topological spaces, compactness, connectedness, quotients and fundamental groups

outcomes.description: Use homotopy, covering-space examples and elementary fundamental-group calculations to distinguish spaces and explain limits of visual intuition.
Construct topologies, subspaces, products and quotients and prove continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation properties.

practice: Analyze glued polygon models, prove a quotient-space property and calculate a fundamental group using a taught van Kampen procedure.

includes: Fourier and Laplace transforms, separation of variables and classical PDE boundary problems

outcomes.description: Solve heat, wave and Laplace boundary/initial-value problems in intervals, rectangles, cylinders and spheres using separation of variables, locally developed Sturm-Liouville theory and Bessel/Legendre eigenfunctions.
Calculate Fourier series, Fourier/Laplace transforms and convolutions; use orthogonality, eigenfunction expansions and stated convergence conditions to solve forced linear problems.

practice: Derive temperature and potential fields in two different geometries and check boundary conditions, dimensions and convergence of truncated expansions.

includes: Variational calculus, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics, constraints and canonical structure

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, calculate Poisson brackets and canonical transformations and analyze rigid-body motion, small oscillations and central-force phase space.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from the action, use generalized coordinates and constraints, and connect continuous symmetries to conserved quantities through a taught Noether argument.

practice: Derive a constrained multibody system in two coordinate choices and show that its conserved quantities and physical trajectories agree.

includes: Observational astronomy, stellar properties, galaxies and accessible cosmological models

outcomes.description: Use sky coordinates, parallax, magnitudes, flux, spectral lines, Doppler shifts and transit/light curves to infer distance, temperature, mass, radius and orbital parameters with degeneracy checks.
Apply locally taught blackbody laws, hydrostatic scaling, nuclear-energy bookkeeping and the empirical Hubble relation to explain stellar evolution, galaxies and evidence for dark components.

practice: Analyze an archival light curve and spectrum to infer a stellar or planetary system and report competing parameter explanations.

includes: DC networks, phasor AC models, bounded RC response and basic electronics
excludes: Semiconductor device theory and differential-equation derivation of transients

outcomes.description: Apply Kirchhoff laws, equivalent circuits and complex impedances to DC and sinusoidal networks; use and interpret a stated exponential RC model, including its initial conditions and limits.
Design a sensor readout with idealized diode, transistor-switch and op-amp models; select grounding, gain, filtering and sampling settings and diagnose loading, clipping and aliasing.

practice: Build or use a circuit simulator to validate an amplifier and RC filter, then collect calibrated sensor data using a meter and oscilloscope.

includes: Crystals, bands, phonons, transport, magnetism and soft/ordered matter

outcomes.description: Calculate lattice normal modes, thermal capacities and Drude transport; analyze bounded spin, elastic and polymer-chain models and interpret evidence for magnetic, liquid-crystalline and superconducting order.

Construct reciprocal lattices and Brillouin zones, derive one-dimensional nearly-free-electron and tight-binding bands and use locally specified Fermi occupation and density-of-states models for metals and semiconductors.

practice: Derive a lattice dispersion and infer material parameters from diffraction, heat-capacity and conductivity datasets, identifying model failures.

includes: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, material response and Maxwell equations

outcomes.description: Use integral and differential Maxwell equations to derive induction, field energy and plane-wave propagation; calculate Lorentz-force motion and energy transfer with stated material models.
Calculate fields and potentials from continuous charge/current distributions; apply symmetry, Gauss/Ampere laws and simple conductor/dielectric boundary conditions in three dimensions.

practice: Solve and compare electrostatic boundary configurations and derive a plane-wave energy balance from Maxwell equations.

includes: Instrument integration, signal extraction, parameter inference and experimental judgment

outcomes.description: Integrate sensors, optics, electronics and data acquisition; teach and implement discrete Fourier analysis, lock-in demodulation and noise spectra with sampling and calibration checks.

Estimate physical parameters using weighted least squares, residuals and a locally taught Jacobian covariance approximation; compare systematic-error models and justify safety, reproducibility and societal-impact decisions.

practice: Complete an optical or electromechanical measurement project with a noise budget, independent calibration, reproducible analysis and an uncertainty-supported conclusion.

includes: Einstein equations, relativistic matter, Schwarzschild geometry and gravitational waves

outcomes.description: Calculate Schwarzschild redshift, orbit precession, light deflection and horizon properties and derive linearized gravitational-wave propagation and detector strain.
Construct stress-energy tensors for particles and perfect fluids, derive geodesic motion variationally and apply Einstein equations and covariant conservation to symmetric metrics.

practice: Derive and compare two observable relativistic corrections and calculate curvature and causal behavior near a Schwarzschild horizon.

includes: Green functions, multipoles, waveguides, radiation and covariant electrodynamics

outcomes.description: Construct electrostatic Green functions and multipole expansions, solve cylindrical/spherical boundary problems and derive guided-wave and dielectric-interface modes.
Derive retarded potentials and dipole radiation, calculate angular power patterns and express Maxwell equations and field transformations in covariant tensor notation taught locally.

practice: Derive a waveguide mode and a radiating-source field, verifying boundary conditions, gauge consistency and energy conservation.

includes: Approximation methods, angular momentum, scattering, density matrices and identical particles

outcomes.description: Derive variational, WKB, degenerate and time-dependent perturbation methods; combine angular momenta and derive central-potential radial solutions using a locally developed Frobenius procedure.
Calculate Born and partial-wave scattering, construct bosonic/fermionic many-particle states and density matrices and analyze reduced states, entanglement and measurement statistics.

practice: Compare variational and numerical bound-state estimates and calculate a scattering observable, including approximation-validity checks.

includes: Calculus-based particle and rigid-body mechanics, conservation and orbits

outcomes.description: Apply work-energy, momentum and angular momentum conservation to collisions, central-force motion and Kepler orbits; infer force parameters from trajectory data.
Formulate vector Newton equations in Cartesian and plane-polar coordinates; calculate trajectories for integrable forces and rotational motion using torque and moment of inertia.

practice: Derive and test an orbital or rotational model, estimating a physical parameter from measured positions or periods.

includes: Special relativity and experimental origins of quantum physics
excludes: General relativity and Schrödinger solution methods

outcomes.description: Analyze photoelectric, Compton, atomic-spectrum and matter-wave evidence using photon and de Broglie relations, distinguishing successful predictions from semiclassical model limitations.
Calculate Lorentz transformations, spacetime intervals, four-momentum conservation and relativistic collision thresholds using an explicitly defined Minkowski metric.

practice: Reconstruct a relativistic collision and estimate physical constants from historical-style photoelectric and spectral data.

includes: Nuclear structure, decay, reactions, particle classification and detector evidence
excludes: Field-theoretic scattering derivations and radiation-handling credentials

outcomes.description: Calculate binding energies, decay chains, tunneling estimates and reaction Q-values using liquid-drop, shell and barrier models; distinguish fission, fusion and decay mechanisms.

Apply conservation laws, relativistic invariant masses and cross-section definitions to particle reactions; interpret tracking, calorimetry and counting data using locally taught efficiency, Poisson-count and background models.

practice: Reconstruct a resonance from simulated detector events and audit energy thresholds, detector efficiency and alternative background explanations.

includes: Geometric optics, scalar interference, diffraction models and optical measurement

outcomes.description: Use locally defined sinusoidal phase addition, two-slit, grating and aperture formulas to calculate interference, resolution and polarization intensity; infer wavelength or size and identify model limits.
Construct ray diagrams and calculate imaging, magnification, reflection, refraction and simple lens-system performance with paraxial assumptions.

practice: Construct a lens or grating measurement and estimate an unknown focal length or wavelength with uncertainty and alignment checks.

includes: Oscillators, normal modes, mechanical waves, acoustics and dispersion

outcomes.description: Derive and solve damped, driven and coupled oscillator equations; calculate resonance, phase and normal modes from mechanical parameters.

Derive the one-dimensional string or acoustic wave equation from force and continuity balances, verify traveling and standing solutions and calculate impedance, reflection, dispersion and energy flux.

practice: Measure resonances in a coupled oscillator or acoustic tube and infer damping and wave speed from amplitude and phase data.

includes: Units, free-body diagrams, constant-acceleration motion, energy and measurement

outcomes.description: Measure length, time, mass and motion; estimate resolution and repeatability, propagate simple independent uncertainties and compare evidence with a model.
Construct free-body diagrams and use algebraic force, pressure, constant-acceleration, momentum and energy models in one and two dimensions.

practice: Measure a rolling or falling object's motion, calibrate the measurement method and justify whether discrepancies exceed measurement uncertainty.

includes: Wavefunctions, operators, finite-state systems, one-dimensional potentials and atomic states
excludes: Full scattering theory and many-body approximations

outcomes.description: Solve one-dimensional wells, barriers and harmonic oscillators; calculate spin measurements, commutators and first-order perturbations and use supplied hydrogen eigenfunctions to interpret three-dimensional atomic quantum numbers.
Normalize complex wavefunctions, calculate continuous probability densities and expectation integrals, use bra-ket notation and Hermitian operators and evolve finite-dimensional states unitarily.

practice: Calculate transmission through a one-dimensional barrier and spin-sequence probabilities, checking normalization, limiting cases and measurement interpretation.

includes: Grand ensembles, quantum gases, interacting models and phase transitions

outcomes.description: Derive mean-field and Landau descriptions of ordering, analyze correlations and critical scaling and implement Metropolis sampling with detailed-balance and finite-size checks.
Derive grand-canonical Bose and Fermi occupations from state counting; calculate blackbody, degenerate-gas and Bose-condensation observables and thermodynamic limits.

practice: Compare a simulated spin-model transition with mean-field predictions and calculate a quantum-gas thermodynamic curve with numerical error control.

includes: Classical ensembles, partition functions, fluctuations and transport models

outcomes.description: Construct microcanonical and canonical ensembles, derive Boltzmann weights and partition-function relations and calculate ideal-gas, oscillator and discrete-spin thermodynamics.
Calculate fluctuations, correlations and response; derive Maxwell velocity distributions and bounded random-walk and kinetic-theory estimates for diffusion and transport.

practice: Derive thermodynamic predictions for a classical model and compare fluctuation or diffusion measurements with the model's microscopic assumptions.

includes: Stellar structure, radiative transfer, compact objects and quantitative cosmology

outcomes.description: Use explicitly stated Friedmann equations and matter/radiation equations of state to calculate expansion histories, distances and horizons; fit bounded cosmological models and assess parameter degeneracies without claiming an Einstein-equation derivation.

Derive and numerically integrate spherical stellar mass, pressure, luminosity and temperature equations using stated opacity and nuclear-rate models; solve one-dimensional radiative transfer and analyze degenerate support.

practice: Implement a stellar-structure shooting calculation and compare expansion-distance predictions with an archival dataset using a supplied least-squares tool.

includes: Temperature, heat, equations of state, thermodynamic laws and heat engines

outcomes.description: Calculate entropy changes and engine or refrigerator performance from reversible reference paths; diagnose irreversibility and distinguish state from path quantities.
Calculate heat, work and internal-energy changes for ideal gases, calorimetry, phase changes and elementary conduction using stated constitutive laws.

practice: Reconstruct an engine cycle from pressure-volume data and audit a thermal-efficiency claim against energy and entropy balances.
